Despite some sources referencing them as husband and wife, the Planner failed to adequately address conflicting information indicating they were not legally married. Notably, the Planner did not direct WebSurfer to explicitly confirm if Leah LaBelle and Rasual Butler were legally married, instead relying solely on superficial language from media outlets without clarifying the details about their marital status. A crucial oversight was that some sources explicitly referred to Rasual Butler as Leah LaBelle’s boyfriend, introducing ambiguity about whether they were officially married. Additionally, none of the searches sufficiently cross-referenced marriage records or authoritative confirmations (e.g., an official marriage registration or legally binding document). This error matches the pattern of "lack of authoritative confirmation" seen in Example 1, where the agent stopped prematurely at ambiguous evidence.
